newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 8.

DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- WALLSALL'S $149M SALE BOOSTS BID EXPECTATION

Wallsall has announced it will be selling its estimated 90m stg stake in General Cable - a sale which will raise its total cashpile to over 300m stg and furthers speculation the group is close to making another acquisition. Analysts, however, have been unable to predict when and where Wallsall, which also owns stakes in households and personal care group McBride and lighting group Thorn Lighting, will make its next purchase.
-- GUINNESS STAKE REDUCED

Bernard Arnault's French luxury goods and spirits company LVMH has reduced its stake in Guinness to 11.99 per cent. The group, which is maintaining its objection to the 24m stg merger between Guinness and Grand Met, sold two million Guinness shares on Thursday, at 591p per share, netting a total of over 11.8m stg in profit.
-- COMPUTING RECRUITER PREDICTS IT STAFF SURGE

Shares in computer and finance recruitment agency Robert Walters rose 14 per cent on Thursday, after the company predicted its interim profits would almost double from 1.7m stg to 3.3m stg and stated it was hoping to be one of the only companies to benefit from the millennium bomb problem. Robert Wallace believes its number of IT contractors will increase dramatically over the next three years, from 150 to 3,000 and that computer consultancy will account for half of its total income by 2000.
THE TIMES
-- TOP CHEF IN HOTEL DEAL WITH GRANADA

The chef known as the 'enfant terrible' of British cooking, Marco Pierre White, has disassociated himself from the Hyde Park Hotel restaurant and signed a two million sterling deal with Granada Group to set up and run seven hotel restaurants over the next 18 months. Mr White has also ended his association with Sir Rocco Forte at whose Balmoral hotel in Edinburgh he was a consultant.
-- SHELL CONFIDENT IN REACHING TARGETS DESPITE CURRENCY LOSSES

Royal Dutch Shell has reported 'disappointing' lower-than-estimated second quarter results, including a 500m stg reduction in profits to 2.5bn stg due to currency losses and problems with its chemicals arm. Shell Transport chairman, Mark Moody-Stuart, stated the company was optimistic about the chemicals business, and its ongoing restructuring should lead to impressive second half results.
-- ZENECA CASTS AN EYE ON OHMEDA

Drugs group Zeneca has expressed a strong interest in acquiring BOH Group's healthcare subsidiary Ohmeda for a reported 1bn stg. Zeneca, which currently distributes Ohmeda's products, faces competition from Smiths Industries, which has also expressed an interest in the Ohmeda. Pre-tax profits at Zeneca rose 10 per cent in the first half to 669m stg, reduced to 579m stg after the impact of sterling was taken into account.
THE GUARDIAN
-- TESCO SUITS BURTON CHIEF

Andrew Higginson, former finance director at Burton Group, has been hired on by Tesco as its new finance director to take the place of David Reid, the company's deputy chairman. Reid will now focus on corporate strategy, information technology, and Tesco's Irish and continental interests. Analysts welcomed the appointment due to Higginson's strong reputation earned during his time at Burton.
-- REED LOOKS AT INTERNET TO PROVIDE PAPER PROFIT

Anglo-Dutch publisher Reed Elsevier has announced that the Internet is having a substantial effect on its paper titles and that its future would be 'heavily influenced by electronics'. Reed director John Mellon said due to an increase in subscriptions, the company now had 2.5bn stg to spend on acquisitions. Interim results at the company included a slight increase in profits to 419m stg and a slight fall in sales to 1.7bn. The strength of the pound caused 117m stg to be taken off sales and 36m stg from profits.
-- ZENECA HIT BY POWER OF THE POUND

Zeneca, the UK pharmaceuticals group run by Sir David Barnes , has urged the government to take a closer look at the impact the strength of sterling is having on businesses and has warned further appreciation in the pound could have serious consequences. Zeneca, which has been relatively safe from the effects of the pound due to its substantial treasury operation, is looking favourably upon the upcoming months, due to the launch of its new oral treatment for migraines, Zomig and plans to expand its specialties operation.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BREWERY CHAINS TO TARGET ALCOPOPS AT ADULT MARKET

Two large UK breweries, Hoopers Hooch-producer Bass and Two Dogs-distributer Scottish Courage, have announced plans to re-market their alcopops beverages to appeal to older customers following moves by supermarkets and Pub chains to ban the sale of the drinks. The decision comes only weeks prior to the introduction of a code of practice concerning the 'young-appeal' drinks by the drinks industry watchdog, the Portman Group.
-- TELEWEST TO DELAY START OF DIGITAL TELEVISION SERVICE

Britain's second-largest cable group, Telewest, has stated it will postpone the launch of its digital television service until spring. According to company chief executive Stephen Davidson, the delay will save 7m stg out of Telewest's 25m stg launch budget and will lead the introduction of its service to coincides with that of BSkyB. For the first six months of 1997, Telewest reported losses of 142.3m stg, up from 117.5m stg during 1996, and announced that its phone customer base had risen to 100,131.
-- SAMSUNG SUFFERS AS CHIP PRICES FALL

Samsung Electronics, the world's leading computer chip manufacturer, has issued a profits warning to its shareholders based on a 'sharp' fall in net profits as reported by group accounting director Choi Hyung Joon. The financial problems have been attributed to a steep decline in global computer chip prices and analysts now predict next Thursday's first half profit announcement will see a figure reduced 75 per cent from that of 1996.
